problem: Prior interactive navigation methods use hand-designed question sets and treat all oracle queries as equally costly, so agents can inflate SR through repeated high-information route questions, and raw SR cannot separate efficient ambiguity resolution from heavy oracle use.
motivation: Instance Goal Navigation is ambiguous from perception and a coarse instruction alone, so asking an oracle is natural, but questions differ greatly in how much information they leak (target confirmation vs route guidance). Interaction therefore needs to be priced and evaluated by efficiency, which requires a taxonomy with data-derived costs and a benchmark that models query cost.
key_idea: Cast interactive IGN as cost-sensitive uncertainty reduction: mine a four-type question taxonomy with corpus-derived costs, evaluate with a cost-discounted Weighted SR, and build a zero-shot MLLM navigator (TANDEM) that asks only when it is worth it and separates planning from metric grounding.
insight: Targeted, typed interaction helps more than unconstrained asking: naive unconstrained QA gives no clear SR gain over the cost-aware protocol but far lower WSR (e.g. GTA 6.4 vs 15.9 WSR@1.5). Ablations show removing QA costs 15.3 SR@1.5 points (35.3 to 20.0) and removing spatial memory costs 7.3, so both matter; the analysis shows Type 3 questions cluster at junctions and corridors and their proxy uncertainty reduction rises from 21.9% (easy) to 47.5% (hard).
method: Question utility mining: a Qwen3.5-4B scorer labels 18,385 balanced records from R2R/REVERIE/RxR/CVDN/SOON with 17 cue types; utility U_c = λ1·avg importance + λ2·high-gain fraction + λ3·rank-1 fraction, mention-weighted per type, rescaled to costs (0.182 appearance, 0.162 region, 0.240 route, 0.103 confirmation).
Weighted SR: episode score = 1{d<=τ}·exp(−Σ w_type(q_i)); repeated questions are charged repeatedly and it reduces to SR when no question is asked.

Isaac Sim benchmark: 22,905 eligible episodes over 262 scenes and 70 categories, with a deterministic difficulty score (distractors, same-room distractors, context ambiguity, start distance). The 500-episode eval subset is split 30:40:30 easy/medium/hard; typed oracle answers are grounded to the target instance.

Planner (MLLM): sees an 8-view panorama, goal, history, remaining question budget, Fact Base and language Spatial Memory, and outputs one decision: ASK(type, question), MOVE(view, place-based subgoal, belief update), or STOP. Cost awareness comes from exposing budget and type penalties in the prompt.

Grounder + executor: the Grounder picks a cell on an 8x8 grid in the selected 90° view; the executor back-projects it via depth or floor-plane geometry to a short waypoint and uses multi-height raycasting (0.6 m) for collision avoidance.

Typed constrained Oracle: Type 1 gives appearance only, Type 2 gives room only, Type 3 gives a natural-language route hint from a 4 m shortest-path front clip plus occupancy metadata (no coordinates or headings), and Type 4 answers yes/no on a visible candidate within 3 m.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-8B (frozen, default); also GPT-5.4, Gemini3-Flash, Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3.5-4B, Gemma-e4B, InternVL3.5-4B
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot); cue-mining and captioning use Qwen3.5-4B offline
setting.observation: 8-view 90° FOV RGB panorama (with depth used by the executor for back-projection), heading, movement history
setting.action_space: semantic decisions (ASK / MOVE direction + subgoal / STOP), grounded to short local waypoints executed by a deterministic controller
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim 4.5 (own benchmark); CVDN/SOON/REVERIE under VLN-MME framework
setting.privileged: Typed oracle access to benchmark metadata (target description, goal room, shortest-path front clip and occupancy metadata for Type 3, visibility checks); the agent gets no GT map or pose beyond its own odometry

numbers_note: The paper's own benchmark is not in the canonical list, so it is labeled 'other:Interactive-IGN (Isaac Sim)' with split 'test' (a fixed 500-episode subset). The CVDN/SOON/REVERIE results are listed as TANDEM zero-shot but beat supervised methods; the paper does not say how it was run there or which backbone, and CVDN 'Val' is mapped to val-unseen without explicit confirmation. Table 3 appears twice in the source with identical content.
results: On the new benchmark under a cost-aware protocol with Qwen3.5-8B, TANDEM reaches 35.3 SR@1.5 and 21.4 WSR@1.5, beating the best adapted baseline GTA (26.0 SR@1.5, 15.9 WSR@1.5). GPT-5.4 raises it to 41.6 SR@1.5 / 25.0 WSR@1.5. It also reports higher numbers than the listed supervised methods on CVDN, SOON and REVERIE (e.g. REVERIE val-unseen SR 62.4 vs ScaleVLN 57.0).
limitations: Assumes idealized sensing and localization (noisy calibration, pose drift and depth holes could break back-projection and raycasting); the real-world pipeline is described but not evaluated.

Question costs derive from a Qwen3.5-4B annotator on VLN corpora as a proxy for information gain, not true posterior information gain, so absolute calibration may be biased; the benchmark is simulated static indoor object search with an LLM oracle.
Repeated MLLM calls make the ask/move/ground loop slow, and the Planner does not use continuous video or richer temporal signals.
